answer: Sybil resistance begins when a requester hands each claimant a peer-issued micro-benchmark sealed with a wall-clock deadline: the job must return a pearl of signed intermediate tensors within 90 seconds, its difficulty tuned to sit at the zenith of one GPU's throughput. A clone silently time-sharing that silicon finishes late, because two tenants cannot split one 80GB HBM die without the deadline exposing the queueing. Verifiers cross-whisper results to peers; any miss slashes the 0.02 ETH bond and drops seat weight. Renting 10,000 genuine GPUs to fake it costs about $18,000 daily.
